mainTopic: No מלקות for a לאו שאין בו מעשה or a לאו שניתק לעשה, the dispute over נותר, and whether a forbidden act takes effect (אביי and רבא)
overview: The גמרא explains that רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's word 'also' adds putting תרומה before ביכורים to the rule that a לאו שאין בו מעשה gets no מלקות. It then asks why a מימר, who also acts only through speech, is flogged. רבי אבין answers that putting תרומה first is a לאו שניתק לעשה, a prohibition that can be fixed by a positive מצוה. אביי challenges רב דימי: תמורה is also fixable, yet it brings lashes. רב דימי answers that תמורה has two לאוין against one עשה. The case of a כהן אונס is set aside because כהנים have extra קדושה. Next, the גמרא shows that whether a לאו with no action brings lashes is a dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי יעקב about נותר of the קרבן פסח. It explains that for רבי יעקב the burning clause teaches a 'second morning' for burning. Finally, אביי and רבא argue whether an act the תורה forbids still takes effect.

steps.title: The word 'also' refers to the exemption from lashes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's 'also' adds the case of putting תרומה before ביכורים to the list of prohibitions with no action, for which there are no מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was talking about the exemption. This is what he meant: for a prohibition that involves no action, one is not flogged. In the name of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא they said: this also includes someone who separates תרומה before ביכורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the earlier question of what the word 'also' was attached to. It says 'also' goes with the rule that there are no lashes for a prohibition done without an action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone could have read 'also' as adding another case where a person IS flogged. The גמרא says no, it adds a case where a person is NOT flogged. Separating תרומה too early involves no physical deed, so it fits the rule of לאו שאין בו מעשה.

keyTerms.meaning: He was standing on, meaning referring to, the exemption
A prohibition broken without any physical action
They give lashes (מלקות)
One who separates תרומה before ביכורים, against the Torah's order

phrases.english: He was referring to the exemption,
phrases.notes: This is the exemption from lashes taught earlier in the name of רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: and this is what he is saying:
a prohibition that has no action in it
one is not flogged for it.

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמְרוּ:
phrases.english: In the name of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina they said:
Also one who separates teruma before the first fruits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question, from before this section, about what 'also' refers to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which rule the word 'also' (אף) in רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's statement is attached to.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is attached to the exemption: putting תרומה before ביכורים is another לאו שאין בו מעשה with no מלקות.

steps.title: Why is one who makes a substitution flogged but not one who separates out of order?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if the person who makes a תמורה is flogged because his speech counts as an action, the same should apply to someone who puts תרומה first.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about someone who makes a substitution, that he is flogged? Is it because his speech counts as an action? Then someone who puts תרומה before ביכורים should also be flogged, because his speech also counts as an action!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction between two cases that seem alike. It asks why one gets lashes and the other does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מימר is flogged even though he only spoke, because his words made the animal holy, so his speech counts as a deed. But separating תרומה is also done by speech and also changes the status of the produce. So the same reasoning should give lashes there too.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? A question pointing out two cases that seem alike
One who makes a substitution (תמורה) of a holy animal
With his speech he did an action; speech that counts as a deed

phrases.english: And what is different about one who substitutes, that he is flogged?
Because with his speech he did an action?
Then one who separates teruma before the first fruits should also be flogged,
because with his speech he did an action!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the exemption just stated by comparing it to the case of תמורה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that one who puts תרומה before ביכורים is not flogged.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both a מימר and a מקדים act only through speech that changes a status. If speech counts as an action for the מימר, it should count for the מקדים too.

steps.title: Separating out of order can be fixed by a positive command
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין answers that putting תרומה first is a לאו שניתק לעשה, and that is why there are no lashes for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין said: That case is different, because it is a prohibition that can be fixed by a positive command, as it is written: 'From all your tithes you shall set apart.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבין gives a different reason why the מקדים is not flogged. The reason is not that he did no action, but that his mistake can be fixed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that a לאו the Torah lets you fix with a positive מצוה afterward does not bring מלקות. The פסוק 'מכל מעשרותיכם תרימו' teaches that even after separating out of order, you must still separate what you skipped. So the speech-as-action idea can still be true, and the two cases are different for another reason.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there; that case has a special reason
A prohibition that can be fixed by a positive command, which brings no lashes
You shall set apart (separate a portion)

steps.whatToRemember: A לאו שניתק לעשה, a prohibition that can be fixed by a positive command, does not bring מלקות. This is why one who separates תרומה before ביכורים is not flogged.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי אבין is not saying the מקדים did no action. He gives a new reason for no lashes: the sin can be fixed. So the case of the מימר is untouched.

phrases.english: Rabbi Avin said: It is different there,
because it is a prohibition that can be fixed by a positive command,
as it is written:
"From all your tithes you shall set apart."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by showing a real difference between the מקדים and the מימר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (שאני התם) by a different legal reason.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מקדים and the מימר are alike, since both act by speech, so both should be flogged.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מקדים is not flogged because his לאו can be fixed by a positive command. The מימר is still flogged; steps 5-6 explain why, even though תמורה also has a fixing עשה.

steps.title: אביי questions whether every fixable prohibition is free of lashes
steps.stepSummary: While רב דימי repeats this teaching, אביי asks whether it is really true that there are never lashes for a לאו שניתק לעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי was sitting and saying this teaching. אביי said to him: And is it true that for every prohibition that can be fixed by a positive command, one is not flogged?
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי teaches רבי אבין's answer, and אביי starts a challenge to it. This step sets up the next move, where אביי will press his point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי is not asking for information. He is doubting the broad rule that every לאו שניתק לעשה gets no lashes. If there are cases where such a לאו does bring מלקות, רבי אבין's answer is in trouble.

keyTerms.meaning: He was sitting (teaching)
A teaching or ruling that was passed on
He is not flogged

phrases.english: Rav Dimi was sitting
and saying this teaching,
phrases.notes: He means רבי אבין's teaching from the last step.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל לָאו שֶׁנִּיתָּק לַעֲשֵׂה לָא לָקֵי?
phrases.english: And for every prohibition that can be fixed by a positive command, one is not flogged?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַב דִּימִי וְקָאָמַר לַהּ לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא, אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the general rule that רבי אבין used in his answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבין's rule that a לאו שניתק לעשה never brings מלקות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אביי doubts the rule applies to every such לאו, which suggests there are cases with lashes even though the sin can be fixed.

steps.title: אביי's proof: the one who makes a substitution is flogged
steps.stepSummary: אביי points to מימר, who is flogged even though his לאו is fixed by an עשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at someone who makes a תמורה. His prohibition is one that is fixed by a positive command, and still he is flogged. We learned in the משנה: it is not that a person is allowed to substitute. Rather, if he does substitute, the substitution takes effect, and he gets the forty lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי backs up his question from step 4 with a concrete case. Someone who makes a תמורה breaks a לאו that has a fixing עשה, and the משנה says he gets lashes anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבין said that a לאו שניתק לעשה gets no מלקות. But the פסוק forbidding תמורה is followed by an עשה: both animals become holy. That should make it a לאו שניתק לעשה, yet the משנה clearly says the person gets forty lashes, so the rule seems to break down.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: the swap works, so the new animal becomes holy too
Receives the forty lashes (מלקות)
Permitted, allowed

phrases.english: But there is one who makes a substitution,
which is a prohibition that is fixed by a positive command,
phrases.notes: The fixing command is in ויקרא 27:10: "it and its substitute shall be holy."

phrases.english: and he is flogged,
as we learned in the Mishnah:
Not that a person is permitted to substitute,
rather, that if he substituted, the substitution takes effect,
and he receives the forty lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מֵימֵר, דְּלָאו שֶׁנִּיתָּק לַעֲשֵׂה הוּא, וְלָקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the case behind אביי's question in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבין's rule that there is no מלקות for a לאו שניתק לעשה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תמורה is a לאו with a fixing עשה, yet the משנה gives lashes for it.

steps.title: Two prohibitions cannot be cancelled by one positive command
steps.stepSummary: תמורה has two לאוין and only one עשה, so the עשה cannot cancel them.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are two prohibitions there and only one positive command. One positive command does not come and uproot two prohibitions.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי answers אביי. תמורה is different because it has two prohibitions, and a single עשה is not strong enough to cancel both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says both "he shall not exchange it" and "nor substitute it", which are two לאוין. There is only one עשה ("it shall be holy"). The rule about לאו שניתק לעשה works only when one עשה balances one לאו, so תמורה keeps its מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: A negative command (a "do not")
A positive command (a "do")
Uproots, cancels

phrases.english: There are two prohibitions there
phrases.notes: Both are in ויקרא 27:10: "he shall not exchange it, nor substitute it."

phrases.english: and one positive command,
and one positive command does not come
and uproot two prohibitions.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: two לאוין against one עשה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: תמורה looked like a normal לאו שניתק לעשה, which should have no lashes.
steps.terutzMaskana: A single עשה cannot cancel two לאוין, so מימר is flogged.

steps.title: Challenge from the rapist who divorces
steps.stepSummary: An אונס has one לאו and one עשה, yet a כהן אונס who divorces is flogged.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at an אונס. He has one prohibition and one positive command, and still the positive command does not uproot the prohibition. It is taught in a ברייתא: an אונס who divorced his victim, if he is a ישראל, takes her back and is not flogged. But if he is a כהן, he is flogged and does not take her back!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 6. In the case of an אונס there is just one לאו and one עשה, yet a כהן is flogged anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says an אונס may never send his wife away (a לאו), and also says "she shall be his wife" (the fixing עשה). A ישראל can remarry her and escapes lashes. A כהן gets lashes even though it is one against one, so the "two against one" answer does not explain everything.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who forced himself on a girl; the תורה requires him to marry her and never divorce her
Takes her back (remarries her)
Is flogged (gets מלקות)

phrases.english: But there is the rapist,
where there is one prohibition and one positive command,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אָתֵי חַד עֲשֵׂה וְעָקַר לָאו,
phrases.english: and the one positive command does not come and uproot the prohibition,
as it is taught:
A rapist who divorced his victim:
if he is a Yisrael,
he takes her back and is not flogged,
and if he is a kohen,
he is flogged and does not take her back!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the "two לאוין against one עשה" answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that one עשה always cancels one לאו and removes מלקות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A כהן אונס has one לאו and one עשה, yet he gets lashes.

steps.title: כהנים are a special case because of their extra holiness
steps.stepSummary: A כהן is flogged for a different reason: the תורה gave כהנים extra קדושה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You bring a proof from כהנים?! כהנים are different for another reason, because the Merciful One gave them extra holiness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the כהן case proves nothing. כהנים are held to a stricter standard because of their extra holiness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that one עשה cancels one לאו still holds, as the Yisrael case shows. The כהן's lashes come from his special holy status, not from any weakness in the rule. So the general principle survives.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning ה׳ or the תורה
Extra holiness
A different reason

steps.whatToRemember: A לאו שניתק לעשה normally gets no מלקות. תמורה is flogged because it has two לאוין against one עשה. A כהן אונס is flogged because of the extra קדושה of כהנים.

phrases.english: You speak of kohanim?!
Kohanim — that is a different reason,
for the Merciful One gave them extra holiness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the כהן אונס.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: a special reason for כהנים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כהן אונס seemed to show that one עשה does not cancel one לאו.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כהן is flogged because of his extra קדושה, so the general rule still stands.

steps.title: Whether a לאו with no action gets lashes is a dispute between תנאים: רבי יהודה on נותר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא in which רבי יהודה says the עשה after the לאו of נותר comes to exempt from lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute among תנאים. On the פסוק 'Do not leave any of it until morning,' the תורה placed an עשה after the לאו to teach that there are no lashes for it. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the rule that a לאו שאין בו מעשה gets no lashes is itself a dispute between תנאים. It starts with רבי יהודה, who exempts נותר from lashes because of the עשה that follows the לאו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לאו is 'do not leave any of the פסח until morning.' The עשה that follows is 'what is left over, burn in fire.' רבי יהודה says the עשה was put there to fix the לאו, so there are no lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: It is like a dispute between תנאים
A positive command placed right after a prohibition
We give lashes
Meat of a קרבן left over past its time

phrases.english: It is like a dispute between תנאים:
"Do not leave any of it until morning"
The verse comes to place a positive command
phrases.notes: The עשה is the rest of the פסוק: whatever is left over, burn it in fire.

phrases.english: after the prohibition,
to say that one is not flogged for it,
these are the words of רבי יהודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the rule from step 1 (no lashes for a לאו שאין בו מעשה) and shows that תנאים argue about it.
steps.raayaObject: That the rule 'לאו שאין בו מעשה אין לוקין עליו' (from step 1) is disputed between תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with רבי יהודה's statement on נותר of the קרבן פסח

steps.title: רבי יעקב gives a different reason: no action was done
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב says there are no lashes for נותר because it is a לאו with no action, not because of the עשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב says: That is not the reason. The reason is that it is a prohibition with no action, and for any prohibition with no action there are no lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב agrees there are no lashes for leaving over the פסח, but he disagrees about the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving meat over is passive, since you just don't eat it. For רבי יעקב, that alone is why there are no lashes, so the עשה is not the reason.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not for that reason

steps.confusionAlert: Both תנאים agree there are no lashes for נותר. They argue only about the reason.

phrases.english: רבי יעקב says:
It is not for that reason,
phrases.notes: He means: the lack of lashes is not because of the עשה.

phrases.english: but rather because it is
a prohibition that has no action,
and any prohibition that has no action,
one is not flogged for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: לֹא מִן הַשֵּׁם הוּא זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No lashes for נותר because it is a לאו שאין בו מעשה, not because of the עשה.

steps.title: Inference: רבי יהודה gives lashes for a לאו with no action
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי יהודה needed the עשה to exempt from lashes, he must hold that a לאו שאין בו מעשה does get lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: We can infer from this that רבי יהודה holds one is flogged for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion about רבי יהודה's view from the way the dispute is set up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a לאו with no action had no lashes anyway, רבי יהודה would not need the עשה to exempt נותר. So he must hold that a לאו שאין בו מעשה normally does get lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference, from what was implied

phrases.english: By inference, רבי יהודה
holds that one is flogged for it.
phrases.notes: 'It' means a לאו with no action, when there is no עשה attached.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר לוֹקִין עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out what רבי יהודה must hold, given רבי יעקב's different reason.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהודה holds that a לאו שאין בו מעשה is punished with lashes, so he needs the עשה to exempt נותר.

steps.title: For רבי יעקב, what is the burning clause for?
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יעקב does not need the עשה to exempt from lashes, what does 'burn the leftover in fire' teach?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יעקב, what does 'and what is left of it until morning, burn in fire' come to teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what purpose the burning clause serves for רבי יעקב, since he does not use it to exempt from lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the clause exists to exempt from lashes. רבי יעקב already has a different reason, so the clause seems to have no job, and the גמרא looks for one.

keyTerms.meaning: What does it come to teach?

phrases.english: And רבי יעקב,
this "and what is left of it until morning
you shall burn in fire"
what does it come for?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב, הַאי ״וְהַנֹּתָר מִמֶּנּוּ עַד בֹּקֶר בָּאֵשׁ תִּשְׂרוֹפוּ״ לְמַאי אֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about רבי יעקב's reading of the פסוק after giving his view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The purpose of the burning clause according to רבי יעקב

steps.title: The clause teaches when to burn the leftovers
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב uses the clause for the משנה's rule that leftovers of the פסח are burned on the 16th, or the 17th if the 16th is שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what we learned in a משנה: The bones, the sinews, and the leftover meat are burned on the sixteenth. If the sixteenth falls on שבת, they are burned on the seventeenth, because burning them does not push aside שבת or יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that for רבי יעקב the burning clause teaches the timing of the burning, which a משנה spells out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 15th of ניסן is יום טוב, so the burning waits until the 16th. If the 16th is שבת, it waits again until the 17th, because burning נותר does not override שבת or יום טוב. So the clause has its own job, and רבי יעקב does not need it to exempt from lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it for (another teaching)
Bones (here, of the קרבן פסח)
Sinews
It does not push aside (שבת or יום טוב)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: no lashes for נותר because of the עשה. רבי יעקב: no lashes because no action is done, and he uses the burning clause to teach when the leftovers are burned.

phrases.english: He needs it for what we learned in a משנה:
The bones, the sinews, and the leftover meat
are burned on the sixteenth.
If the sixteenth falls on שבת,
they are burned on the seventeenth,
because they do not push aside

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת וְלֹא אֶת יוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: either שבת or יום טוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by giving the clause a different purpose.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The burning clause teaches the timing of burning נותר (the 16th, not on שבת or יום טוב), as taught in the משנה.

steps.title: The verse gives a second morning for burning
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה, backed by a teaching from his school, shows that the פסוק about burning נותר allows the burning to be done on a second morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said, and his school also taught this: what is the source? The פסוק says 'and what is left of it until morning you shall burn in fire.' The verse is giving a second morning for the burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source in the פסוק for the rule from the previous step. That rule says leftovers can be burned later if the first day is שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse mentions 'morning' twice. Since the first 'morning' already set the deadline, the extra 'morning' is read as a second, later morning on which the burning may happen. This shows that רבי יעקב's use of the clause is anchored in the text.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse (a פסוק in the תורה)
A second morning
Burning

phrases.english: And חזקיה said,
and so the school of חזקיה taught:
What is the reason?
The verse says:
"And what is left of it until morning
you shall burn in fire."
The verse comes to give
a second morning for its burning.
phrases.notes: The פסוק says 'morning' twice, so the second one is read as an extra morning when you may burn it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the verse-based source for the משנה's rule that רבי יעקב attached to the clause in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that leftovers may be burned on a later day when the first day is שבת or יום טוב
steps.raayaSupportSource: The double mention of 'morning' in שמות 12:10, as taught by חזקיה and his school
steps.whatToRemember: The second 'morning' in the פסוק teaches that burning נותר can wait for a second morning. This closes the discussion of what the clause teaches according to רבי יעקב.

steps.title: אביי: a forbidden act still takes effect
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that whenever the תורה forbids an action and someone does it, the action still works. He proves this from the fact that the person gets lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: anything the תורה said 'do not do,' if a person did it, it works. For if you think it does not work, why does he get lashes?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. אביי states a general rule: an action the תורה forbids still takes effect if someone does it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי reasons that lashes only make sense if the person actually accomplished something. If the forbidden act did nothing at all, there would be nothing to punish, so the act must have worked.

keyTerms.meaning: It is effective; it takes effect
He receives lashes
If it enters your mind (if you were to think)

phrases.english: אביי said:
Any matter about which the Merciful One said
"do not do it,"
if one did it, it is effective.
For if you think it is not effective,
why does he get lashes?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: כֹּל מִילְּתָא דְּאָמַר רַחֲמָנָא לָא תַּעֲבֵיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: whether a forbidden act takes effect. This ties back to the earlier case of תמורה, which takes effect and also brings lashes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A forbidden act takes effect, and the person still gets lashes.
steps.confusionAlert: 'It works' does not mean 'it is allowed.' אביי agrees the act is forbidden and the person gets lashes. He is only saying the result still counts.
steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute between אביי and רבא is one of the most famous in the גמרא and is used across many areas of הלכה.

steps.title: רבא: a forbidden act does not take effect
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees. A forbidden act accomplishes nothing, and the lashes are only for disobeying the תורה's command.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: it does not work at all. And the reason he gets lashes is because he went against the word of the Merciful One.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the opposite view to אביי. He also answers אביי's proof from lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי assumed lashes require that something was achieved. רבא says the punishment is for the disobedience itself, so it makes no difference that the act changed nothing. This removes the basis of אביי's proof.

keyTerms.meaning: It does not take effect at all
He transgressed; he went against
The word (command) of the Merciful One

phrases.english: רבא said:
It is not effective at all.
And the fact that he gets lashes
is because he transgressed
the word of the Merciful One.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to אביי and answers his proof from lashes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A forbidden act does not take effect. The lashes are for disobeying ה׳'s command.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי says a forbidden act works and the lashes prove it. רבא says it does not work, and the lashes are just for disobeying the תורה.
